title: The library holds 266 scenarios with no structural problems
steps: Load shared/scenarios/index.js
Read SCENARIOS and SCENARIO_PROBLEMS
expected: SCENARIOS has 266 records: the original 166 plus the 100 new ones
SCENARIO_PROBLEMS is empty
Every case file built from a scenario passes validateCase

title: The original 166 scenarios are unchanged
steps: Import the 20 original data files (uk.js to other.js) in index order
Hash JSON.stringify of the combined list with SHA-256
expected: 166 records
SHA-256 fingerprint b035f77f067c01b2b1b4ab8c58e65760da8fd657fe4303b079dd36cf49f8d60e

title: Every scenario has a valid claim stage
steps: Check each scenario’s stage against STAGES
Check where each stage comes from
expected: All 266 have a stage from the 10 in STAGES
The original 166 take theirs from shared/scenarios/stages.js and their records have no stage field
The 100 new records carry stage themselves

title: New scenario ids continue each country’s series without gaps
steps: List the ids of the 100 new scenarios by country
expected: No id or title repeats an existing one

title: The new scenarios keep the country mix
steps: Count the 100 new scenarios by country
expected: UK 22, US 20, India 22, other countries 36 (Canada 5, Australia 5, UAE 4, Germany 4, France 4, South Africa 4, Singapore 4, and one each for Ireland, New Zealand, Japan, Italy, Spain, Malaysia)

title: The new scenarios cover all four claim areas
steps: Count the 100 new scenarios by stage and stage group
expected: Intake and cover 22, Assessment and settlement 20, Third parties, recovery and legal 31, Fraud, compliance and customer 27
Every one of the 10 stages has at least 6 new scenarios

title: The Claim stage filter is offered with grouped options
steps: Read FILTERS
Open the library in the browser and open the Claim stage list
expected: 11 filters; Claim stage is second, after Country
Its 10 options appear under 4 group headings: Intake and cover; Assessment and settlement; Third parties, recovery and legal; Fraud, compliance and customer
With no filters set, the stage counts add up to 266

title: Filtering by one stage returns exactly that stage
steps: queryScenarios with filters { stage: [stage] } for each stage
expected: Coverage 53, Fraud 45, Third-party 44, Assessment 33, Settlement 24, Recovery 21, Notification 17, Legal 14, Customer 9, Compliance 6
Every result has the requested stage

title: Stage combines with other filters and facets stay consistent
steps: queryScenarios with { stage: ["fraud"], country: ["IN"] }
facetCounts with { stage: ["fraud"] }
expected: 10 results, all Indian fraud-stage scenarios
The stage facet ignores its own filter (other stages still show counts)
Other facets add up to the 45 fraud-stage scenarios

title: Search finds the new scenarios by their key concepts
steps: Search for: Part 36; SASRIA; time-limited demand; Werkstattrisiko; subject access request; Enhanced Care; knock-for-knock; family violence; insider fraud; Cashless Treatment Scheme

title: Search matches stage names
steps: Search for "regulatory compliance"
Search for "ombudsman"
expected: "regulatory compliance" returns the compliance-stage scenarios
"ombudsman" lists IN-057 first

title: Existing search behaviour is unchanged
steps: Run the existing search assertions against the 266-scenario library
expected: "UK crash for cash" lists UK-021 first and only UK scenarios
"kangaroo" lists AU-001 first
"pay and recover" (quoted) returns exactly IN-010 and IN-025
"FIR" returns only Indian scenarios
"EV fire" returns at most 6 scenarios, including UK-014 and IN-018

title: GET /api/scenarios filters by stage
steps: GET /api/scenarios?stage=legal&limit=200
expected: 200 OK
total is 14 and every item has stage "legal"
Each item summary includes stage

title: GET /api/scenarios returns stage facets
steps: GET /api/scenarios
expected: facets.stage has the 10 stages and adds up to 266
total is 266

title: GET /api/scenarios/:id returns a new scenario with its case file
steps: GET /api/scenarios/in-048 (lower case)
expected: 200 OK
scenario.id is IN-048 and scenario.stage is "third-party"
The case file has the notification, statement, accounts and evidence exhibits

title: GET /api/scenarios/random honours the stage filter
steps: GET /api/scenarios/random?stage=compliance ten times
expected: Every scenario returned has stage "compliance"

title: The detail page shows the claim stage and filters by it
steps: Open #/scenarios/UK-057
Find Claim stage in the facts
Click the stage value
expected: Claim stage shows "Regulatory compliance"
Clicking it opens the library filtered to that stage (6 scenarios)
The nine facts sit in three rows of three on desktop and two columns at 390 px wide

title: Case files never reveal the reference answers or the stage
steps: Build the case file for each of the 100 new scenarios
expected: No case file contains whatHappened, assessment or action text
No case file contains the stage label
No missing item appears as held evidence

title: Assessing a new scenario streams a result with the comparison
steps: POST /api/scenarios/UK-037/assess with a test provider
In the browser with a real key: open UK-037 and run the AI assessment
expected: NDJSON stream with progress messages and one result
result.scenarioId is UK-037 and result.comparison has overall, intent and risk
In the browser the comparison card shows agrees, close or differs

title: The evaluation runner works without a model
steps: node scripts/run-evals.mjs --dry-run
node scripts/run-evals.mjs --oracle
expected: Dry run checks 125 case files with no errors
Oracle run passes 100 of 100 scenario cases
Each run writes results.json and report.md

title: Every AI test case is well formed
steps: Check AI_CASES with caseProblems
expected: 125 cases, TC-001 to TC-125 in order
100 scenario cases cover the 100 new scenarios once each
Every case has valid families and risks and at least one required check

title: Counterfactual patches apply cleanly and required checks are not in the case file
steps: Apply each counterfactual patch
Compare every required phrase with the case file text
expected: Each find text occurs exactly once and the patched case file is valid
No required phrase appears in its case file, so a check passes only when the assessment adds the concept

title: The grader passes good answers and fails weak ones
steps: Grade each scenario’s reference answer
Grade an answer that only repeats the case file
Grade an answer with the wrong intent family
expected: All 100 reference answers pass
The repeat-the-file answers fail every case
A wrong family fails even when every concept is present

title: The stage filter works on a phone-sized screen
steps: Open the library at 390 px wide
Open the filters and choose a stage
Clear it with the filter chip
expected: The grouped list is readable and selectable
The chip shows the stage name and removes the filter

title: Both builds include the new scenarios
steps: npm run build
npm run build:artifact
Open the hosted build and search for SASRIA
expected: Both builds finish without errors
The hosted build shows 266 scenarios and finds ZA-008
